title: Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: State Differences and Salary Packaging Perth
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary with a 38-hour week, including state differences in ordinary-time earnings and how salary packaging Perth affects take-home pay.
salarySummary: Annual gross pay is hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming 38 hours per week for full-time work, with superannuation paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full‑time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year. This is gross pay before tax and super. Super is paid on top of this amount at 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and an award rate?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026 it is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). Award rates are set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries or occupations and are often higher. Casual employees also receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. Always check your award or agreement for the correct minimum pay.

faqs.q: Does salary packaging affect how I calculate my annual salary?
faqs.a: Salary packaging (or salary sacrifice) lets you pay for certain items with pre‑tax income, which reduces your taxable income. However, our annual salary estimate does not include salary packaging. If you use salary packaging, your take‑home pay may differ from the estimate. For more details, see our guide on super and packaging. Salary packaging Perth is common in sectors like healthcare and mining, but the calculation of gross annual pay remains the same.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Hourly Pay to Annual Salary: What You Need to Know

If you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, understanding the annual equivalent is essential for comparing jobs, budgeting, and planning your tax. The basic formula is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full‑time employee, we assume a standard 38‑hour week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. This gives you a gross annual figure before tax, super, and any other deductions.

### The Formula and Why 38 Hours Matters

Most full‑time roles in Australia are based on 38 ordinary hours per week. To convert your hourly rate:

- **Annual gross** = hourly rate × 38 × 52
- **Fortnightly gross** = hourly rate × 38 × 2 (or annual ÷ 26)

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. The fortnightly amount is $2,009.44. If you work part‑time or different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

It’s important to know which pay rate applies to you:

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44 per hour (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement.
- **Award rates**: Many industries have specific awards that set higher minimum pay rates. Check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive an extra 25% on top of the base rate. For the minimum wage, that’s $33.05 per hour. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** into the timesheet – use the checkbox to add it.
- **Superannuation**: The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid **on top** of your gross pay. It does not reduce your take‑home pay but is an additional contribution to your retirement fund. The maximum earnings base for super is $270,830 per year.

### State Differences in Ordinary‑Time Earnings

While the national average weekly ordinary‑time earnings for full‑time adults was $2,083.70 in May 2026 (ABS), earnings vary across states and territories. For instance, Western Australia often reports higher average earnings due to its mining and resources sector. However, these are **averages**, not medians for a specific job. Your actual pay depends on your award, enterprise agreement, or individual contract.

If you are considering a role in Perth, you may also explore **salary packaging perth** options. Salary packaging (or salary sacrifice) allows you to pay for certain items – such as a car, laptop, or super contributions – with pre‑tax income, reducing your taxable income. This can affect your take‑home pay, but our annual estimate does not include it. For more information, see our page on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Once you have your gross annual salary, you can estimate your tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). Note that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted in this estimate.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It calculates your annual, fortnightly, and weekly gross pay, plus an estimate of tax and super. For a deeper look at how your pay compares, see our [reference tables](/data) or [pay guides](/blog). If you want to understand take‑home pay after tax, visit [take-home pay](/topics/take-home).

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Final Thoughts

Whether you are negotiating a salary, comparing job offers, or budgeting, converting your hourly rate to an annual figure gives you a clear picture. Remember to check your award or agreement for the correct rate, and consider state differences if you are moving interstate. For those in Perth, **salary packaging perth** may offer tax advantages, but it does not change the gross annual calculation. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide for more examples, and always consult a professional for personalised advice.
